newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs seen treading water ahead Buba, U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OLOs seen treading water ahead Buba, U.S. data.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) were expected to tread water while digesting new supply ahead of Thursday's Bundesbank meeting and U.S. producer price data on Friday, dealers said.
"I think we are in for a quiet couple of days," one said, saying no-one expected a move in German interest rates. The U.S. September PPI is seen rising 0.3 percent from August.
OLOs ended firmer on Tuesday, buoyed by a rise in German unemployment, with the benchmark 2006 yield falling to 6.09 from 6.11 percent late on Monday.

But OLOs lagged Bunds, with the spread widening slightly to 12 from 10 basis points after starting the day narrower at nine basis points. One dealer noted the market tends to underperform Germany in up moves.

Another said the market was weighed on by a Treasury auction, at which 14.4 billion Belgian francs of shorter dated OLOs were exchanged for longer-dated maturities. 6.5 billion francs was in the March 2007 paper which is destined next year to become Belgium's new benchmark.
But dealers said they were not worried by the small move in the spread.

"The big question is whether it is going to head toward zero or go out again," one trader said. He said he would feel more comfortable with a spread between 15 and 20 basis points but did not expect this to happen in the near future.
"For the moment Belgium remains well bid," he said, noting domestic investors continued to favour five to eight year paper.
